title: Run through a binary register
statement: Let $P$ be a register program with oracle, and let $r_1,r_2$ be distinct registers. Suppose the transition at state $e_B$ performs the binary comparison step for $r_1$, leading to $l$ when the scanned bit is blank and otherwise moving left while remaining at $e_B$, and suppose $e_B$ is not a call state. If the contents of register $r_1$ initially store the word $w_1$, then for every natural number $n$ and integer $p$ with $p+1=n$ and $p<|w_1|$, running for $n+1$ steps from state $e_B$ with both register heads at position $p$ reaches state $l$ with both heads at position zero. At every earlier time $t<n+1$, the configuration has state $e_B$ and both heads at some integer position $q$ with $-1\le q\le p$.
hypotheses_covered: Transition at $e_B$ has the specified binary-comparison behavior
